slides.title: Full dataset: held-out CV over λ × k
bullets: All 16,460 cells × 19,543 detected genes (322 M entries), 5% (16.1 M) held out. Best λ=10, k=40: NLL 0.1778, AUC 0.965 vs 0.1854 / 0.962 for cell + gene logistic. Refit on all entries: 188 PG-EM iterations, J monotone.

slides.title: Full dataset: every cell × every detected gene
bullets: At this scale most of the 19,543 genes are rarely detected, so area-averaged views are dominated by broadly expressed genes; P̂ tracks detection density across the whole matrix.

slides.title: Full dataset: all cells × 40 marker genes per hemilineage
bullets: 920 genes most enriched per hemilineage. The block diagonal appears in counts, binary Y and P̂; P̂ fills dropouts inside each block.

slides.title: Full dataset: zoom, every entry visible
bullets: 10 cells per hemilineage × 3 marker genes per hemilineage (23 hemilineages). Sparse detections become consistent within-type probabilities.

slides.title: UMAPs: processed counts vs binary Y vs BernFac P̂
bullets: Rows: processed counts (R1), binary Y (R2), BernFac P̂ (R3); columns coloured by hemilineage, library, depth. R1 gives tight, separated hemilineage islands; R2 and R3 resolve hemilineages at the periphery but keep a depth gradient that mixes a central mass.

slides.title: Which representation reflects biology best?
bullets: Processed counts (R1) win on every hemilineage metric (kNN 0.98, Leiden ARI 0.65, purity 0.97) and mix libraries best. BernFac P̂ retains a depth axis (|ρ| 0.98, no cell offset); removing it lifts R3 ARI 0.49 → 0.61, still below R1.
